editions.briefing: An Army plan to detonate Iowa explosives proceeds despite a court order, and COP31 climate talks collapsed over fossil fuels. President Trump told federal contractors to clear replies to Congress. Google staff joined protests over AI in school search, and Signal limited mobile screenshots. UK energy bills are set to jump in January, and Medicare open enrollment ends Dec. 7. In Idaho, San Diego State upset Boise State 22-20.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, and the FBI is reportedly investigating an apparent hack of its criminal database. An Anthropic staffer claims he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, though the claim has yet to be verified. In business, an Ohio steel mill dropped a plan to cut coal use, and the ICE detention of a Princeton researcher worried international scholars. In Idaho, health officials want a 13% raise for disability caregivers.

COP31 climate talks in Turkey are deadlocked over fossil fuels, and UN talks on killer robots ended without binding rules. Nasdaq fell 10% for the week as the AI boom showed strain, with Anthropic closing near its IPO price. A judge approved a $7.25bn Roundup settlement, and the UK and EU agreed a trade deal. A jury convicted the man behind the Palisades Fire. In Idaho, a state report tied prison growth to drug charges.

President Trump called his Asia trip a success despite few concrete results, and a second judge moved to block his planned arch. The White House fired its national cyber director after tech outages. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in an AI stock sell-off, entering a correction. An Anthropic mathematician claimed a Riemann hypothesis proof, still unverified. In Idaho, lawmakers plan a bill to regulate e-motos.

The US and Iran traded strikes across the Gulf, with drones reported near bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate race, and Xi greeted Trump at the APEC summit. OpenAI released GPT-6.2, and Anthropic's IPO is reportedly set to price this week. HHS finalized a HIPAA records rule, and the US lost measles elimination status. In Idaho, a Fish and Game commissioner will plead guilty in a poaching case.
